quick_ref.Theme: Time Detective Agency — Case File: My Weekend
quick_ref.Grammar Focus: Review: Past Simple (Regular verbs & was/were) + Sequence Words

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Project-Based Review
content: Problem: Students often forget past tense structures when trying to tell a longer, connected story.

Solution: This week introduces no new grammar. Instead, it consolidates Block B learning (Past Simple, feelings, sequence words) through a hands-on project: creating a 4-panel comic strip. The visual panels anchor the chronological sequence ("First", "Then") and emotional states ("was happy").

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Review past simple verbs and sequence words. Draft Panels 1 & 2 of the comic.
Session 2: Review "was/were" and emotion adjectives. Draft Panels 3 & 4.
Session 3: Finalize the comic strip and practice the oral presentation.

methodology.title: 2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Student picks a sequence card ("First") and a verb card ("played"), then makes a full past tense sentence.
S2 pull-out: Show an emotion flashcard. Student says "I was [feeling]" and gives one past tense reason (e.g., "I was tired. I cleaned my room.").
Communicative task (Step 5): Information Gap. Student A has Panel 1 and 3 of a mystery comic. Student B has Panel 2 and 4. They must ask questions to complete the story sequence.

parts.title: PART 6: STEM/CLIL — How to Make a Comic
content: Read this: A comic tells a story using pictures and words. It uses panels (boxes) to show time passing. The first panel shows what happened first. The next panels show what happened after that. Drawing a comic helps you plan a story in your brain. You draw the action, and then you write the words!

content: Luna is finishing her comic strip. She wants to show her feelings. In panel three, she draws her face. She writes, "Next, I watched a movie with my sister. I was happy." games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W26: played, helped, watched, happy, tired
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (played, helped, watched, happy, tired) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Review: Past Simple (Regular verbs & was/were) + Sequence Words
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Review: Past Simple (Regular verbs & was/were) + Sequence Words.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Memories — Review & Project 2 (My Weekend Comic)"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Memories — Review & Project 2 (My Weekend Comic)".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (played, helped, watched, happy, tired usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

chanting.title: Chanting — W26 (9 prompts)
chanting.script:

STEM/CLIL Extension Notes (teacher only):

PART 6: STEM/CLIL CONNECTION
How to Make a Comic
Read this: A comic tells a story using pictures and words. It uses panels (boxes) to show time passing. The first panel shows what happened first. The next panels show what happened after that. Drawing a comic helps you plan a story in your brain. You draw the action, and then you write the words!
Write 2 sentences applying the CLIL concept:
A comic uses panels to show ____________________________________________________________
First, you draw the action, and then you ____________________________________________________________
[O Bonus]: Why are panels important in a comic? ____________________________________________________________

STEM/CLIL Extension Notes (teacher only):

PART 6: STEM/CLIL CONNECTION
Drawing Emotions
Read this: In a comic, artists draw faces to show feelings. This helps the reader understand the story quickly. To show "happy," you draw a curve pointing up. To show "tired," you draw small lines under the eyes and a straight mouth. The face matches the action in the panel!
